answer: Unique-work claim ledger. Each agent identity must submit a solution to a fresh randomly generated task whose output is verified in one pass but whose search cannot be shortcut or reused; a solved instance is retired. The ledger stores a jade hash of each answer, and a duplicate or near-duplicate claim is rejected at the harbor gate before registration. Attackers pay full compute per identity with no reuse, making mass sybils linearly costly in timber and machine time.
